question: What is the value of (sqrt{121} + sqrt{49})²
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate the **square roots** of the given numbers: √121 = 11 and √49 = 7.

Add the values: 11 + 7 = 18.

Find the **square** of the sum: 18² = 324.

**∴ The correct answer is 324.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (√121 + √49)²

**Formula Used:**

Basic **Arithmetic Operations** and **Square Roots**.

⇒ (√121 + √49)²

⇒ (11 + 7)²

⇒ (18)²

⇒ 18 × 18

⇒ 324

**∴ The correct answer is 324.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares and Roots

A **perfect square** is an integer that is the square of an integer; for example, 121 is 11² and 49 is 7².

Algebraic Identity

The expression can also be expanded using (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, where a = √121 and b = √49.

Common Squares

Memorizing squares up to 30 helps in **fast calculation**: 17² = 289, 18² = 324, 19² = 361, 20² = 400.</p
